alerts.reason: Socket identifies a maintenance upgrade opportunity, not a vulnerability. The package is transitive to the release-tested Satori peer through @shuding/opentype.js, and this baseline does not establish a compatible upstream Satori update that removes it. The 0.6.0 evaluation of string.prototype.codepointat@1.0.1 through an npm override returned the same Socket scores and alert set while growing the lockfile from 700 to 773 packages, so the override remains rejected as a net-negative supply-chain change.

alerts.reason: Socket flags packed data, not hidden behavior. caniuse-lite 1.0.30001828, published 2026-11-24 by GitHub Actions with an SLSA v1 provenance attestation, replaced its data encoding: data/versionGroups.js and dist/unpacker/versionGroups.js were removed, data/featureSupport.js (an array of support bit flags) and data/regionVersions.js were added, each data/features/*.js entry now holds a run-length string over printable ASCII, and dist/unpacker/feature.js, agents.js, and region.js were rewritten to decode it. The decoder is documented in its own comments (tokens 0-34 index featureSupport, 35-37 prefix rarer values, 38-92 are bijective base-55 run lengths) and its only identifier resembling obfuscation is a parameter named cipher holding the bit flags. A diff of the 1.0.30001809 and 1.0.30001828 tarballs found no eval, Function constructor, network, filesystem, child_process, or process.env use in any file. metaplate has no runtime dependencies and does not ship caniuse-lite; the lockfile reaches it only through the optional next peer and the development-only @react-router/dev fixture's Babel toolchain (browserslist), never through the required satori, @resvg/resvg-js, or react peers. The lockfile was moved from 1.0.30001809 to 1.0.30001828 so this disposition covers the version Socket resolved. Re-evaluate at the next Socket baseline capture.
